judge.summary: Yes—with a material reliability caveat. The AI used simulator-only verified fixture evidence to identify and contextualize a possible value compromise, resumed customer-facing selling, detected genuine viewing intent, and made an appropriately timed appointment handoff with little or no sales work remaining. It did not claim availability or treat the customer’s interest as a confirmed appointment. However, it made repeated availability support requests even though the fixture did not provide availability, and it did not explore the large difference between the buyer’s stated budget and the quoted figure. The RM349,000 unit/package details are SIMULATOR_SYNTHETIC_VERIFIED_FIXTURE evidence only—not Pearlmont Knowledge or evidence of live inventory or package capability. The human executor could not verify availability or package validity, so the operational task was not completed; this does not negate the AI’s appointment-ready handoff outcome.
judge.improvement_recommendation: Prevent duplicate support requests for an unresolved question when the prior verified result does not answer it. After one unsuccessful availability check, state that availability remains unverified and proceed to the appropriate operational handoff once the buyer is ready. Also clarify the buyer’s price basis when a returned figure differs substantially from their stated budget. Source target: MISSING_SOURCE.
